caption: What if you were a tardigrade? These tiny 'water bears' have 8 chubby legs and are usually under 1 millimetre long, yet they live in moss almost everywhere on Earth, even about 5,500 metres up in the Himalayas. Their superpower: they dry out into a little ball called a tun and almost pause life. Tardigrades from Antarctic moss that sat frozen for over 30 years woke up and laid eggs. About 5 to 10 Gy of radiation can kill a human, while lab tardigrades survived around 5,000 Gy. In 2007, dried tardigrades spent 10 days exposed to open space on a satellite, and many came back alive. The plot twist: awake, active tardigrades are surprisingly sensitive to heat. In a 2020 lab study, a day at about 37 °C killed half of them, and summer afternoons in much of India often go past that. Would YOU swap places with a water bear? 👇
